title: Churros
description: Churros are a classic Spanish-style fried pastry known for their deeply crisp ridged exterior, tender and lightly airy center, delicate cinnamon-sugar coating, and rich chocolate dipping sauce. The professional texture comes from properly cooked choux-style dough, controlled egg incorporation, a large star nozzle, and frying at a precise temperature.

ingredients.title: For the Churros Dough
items: Whole eggs – 100 g (approximately 2 large eggs), beaten
Orange zest – finely grated from ½ orange, optional

ingredients.title: For Frying
items: Neutral cooking oil such as sunflower, canola, or refined peanut oil – approximately 1.5–2 litres

ingredients.title: For the Chocolate Dipping Sauce
items: Dark chocolate, 60–70% cocoa – 100 g, finely chopped
Glucose syrup or mild honey – 15 g

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Churros Dough
steps: Combine water, whole milk, butter, neutral oil, sugar, and salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Heat over medium heat until the mixture reaches a full simmer and the butter has completely melted.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and immediately add all of the sifted flour at once.
Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon or heatproof spatula until no dry flour remains and a smooth dough forms.
Return the saucepan to medium-low heat and cook the dough for approximately 1½–2 minutes, stirring continuously.
Continue cooking until the dough pulls away cleanly from the sides of the pan and a thin film forms on the bottom.
Do not skip this drying stage, as excess moisture can produce greasy or poorly structured churros.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Incorporating the Eggs
steps: Transfer the hot dough to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment.
Mix on low speed for 2–3 minutes to release excess steam and allow the dough to cool slightly.
Gradually add the beaten eggs in several additions, mixing thoroughly after each addition.
Add vanilla extract and optional finely grated orange zest.
Continue mixing until the dough becomes smooth, glossy, and homogeneous.
The finished dough should be firm enough to retain the shape of a star nozzle and should fall slowly from the paddle in a thick ribbon.
Do not add all the egg automatically if the dough has already reached the correct consistency; the exact absorption can vary slightly with flour and egg size.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Piping and Shaping
steps: Transfer the churros dough into a strong piping bag fitted with a large closed-star nozzle approximately 12–15 mm in diameter.
Pipe the dough into 12–14 cm lengths onto parchment paper or directly over the frying oil.
For consistent restaurant presentation, pipe uniform lengths and thicknesses.
If using parchment squares, pipe one churro onto each square and keep the dough covered until frying.
Avoid making the churros excessively thick, as the center may remain undercooked before the exterior becomes properly crisp.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Frying the Churros
steps: Heat the frying oil to approximately 175–180°C in a deep, heavy-bottomed pan or commercial fryer.
Carefully place the churros into the hot oil without overcrowding the frying vessel.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature remains stable.
Fry for approximately 3–4 minutes, turning the churros occasionally for even browning.
Maintain the oil close to 175°C throughout frying. Avoid allowing the temperature to remain significantly below 170°C, as the churros may absorb excess oil.
Avoid temperatures above approximately 185°C, as the exterior can brown too quickly while the interior remains undercooked.
Continue frying until the churros are deeply golden, crisp, and visibly ridged.
Remove with a spider or slotted utensil and drain briefly on a wire rack.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Cinnamon Sugar Coating
steps: Combine superfine sugar, ground cinnamon, and a small pinch of sea salt in a wide bowl or tray.
While the churros are still hot, transfer them directly into the cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Roll gently until the entire surface is evenly coated.
Shake off excess sugar and place the churros on a wire rack or serving tray.
For the best texture, serve the churros within a few minutes of frying.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Preparing the Chocolate Sauce
steps: Finely chop the dark chocolate and place it in a heatproof bowl.
Combine heavy cream and glucose syrup or honey in a saucepan.
Heat until the cream reaches a gentle simmer without allowing it to boil aggressively.
Pour the hot cream mixture over the chopped chocolate and allow it to stand for approximately 1 minute.
Whisk slowly from the center outward until the chocolate and cream form a smooth, glossy emulsion.
Add butter, vanilla, and sea salt and whisk until completely incorporated.
Keep the sauce warm at approximately 40–45°C for service.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Restaurant-Style Finishing
steps: Arrange 3–4 freshly fried churros on a warm dessert plate.
Serve with warm dark chocolate dipping sauce in a small ramekin or sauce vessel.
For a premium presentation, add a small spoonful of dulce de leche or salted caramel.
Optional: garnish with finely grated orange zest, a light dusting of cinnamon, or a few flakes of sea salt.
Serve immediately while the churros are crisp and the chocolate sauce remains warm.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve freshly fried and warm with thick dark chocolate dipping sauce.
Pair with dulce de leche, salted caramel, or vanilla pastry cream.
For a plated restaurant dessert, serve with vanilla, cinnamon, or malted milk ice cream.
Serve alongside espresso, café con leche, or strong black coffee.
For a Spanish-inspired presentation, serve with warm thick drinking chocolate.
For individual portions, serve 3–4 medium churros per person with a separate dipping sauce.

chefTips: Cook the flour mixture on the stovetop before adding the eggs. Properly drying the dough is essential for a crisp exterior and stable interior.
Do not add the eggs while the dough is extremely hot, as excessive heat can partially cook the eggs and produce an uneven dough.
Add the eggs gradually. The exact amount absorbed can vary depending on flour, egg size, and how thoroughly the dough was dried.
Use a large closed-star nozzle. The ridges increase the surface area, creating the characteristic crisp texture and allowing the churros to cook more evenly.
Do not use a small round nozzle for professional churros, as the resulting smooth surface will not provide the same crisp ridged texture.
Maintain frying oil at approximately 175–180°C. Temperature control is one of the most important factors in achieving a crisp, non-greasy churro.
Avoid overcrowding the fryer, as adding too many churros at once can cause a significant temperature drop and increase oil absorption.
Use a wire rack rather than placing the churros directly on paper towels for an extended period. A rack allows steam to escape and helps preserve the crisp crust.
Coat the churros in cinnamon sugar immediately after frying while the surface is still hot and slightly oily so the sugar adheres evenly.
For a refined flavor profile, add a small amount of orange zest to the dough or cinnamon sugar.
Use good-quality dark chocolate with approximately 60–70% cocoa for a balanced sauce that is rich without becoming excessively sweet.
For an especially glossy chocolate sauce, whisk the butter into the finished ganache at the end rather than boiling it with the cream.
The finished churro should have a deeply golden, crisp, ridged exterior and a tender, lightly airy interior without being doughy or greasy.
For commercial or restaurant production, standardize the piped length and dough weight so frying time and portion size remain consistent.
Churros are at their peak immediately after frying; avoid holding them for long periods before service.
For a premium restaurant version, finish with warm chocolate crémeux, salted caramel, vanilla ice cream, and a small amount of flaky sea salt.
